claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
The 2026 predictions from last year's edition of this piece held up.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and described cloud as becoming a business necessity.
According to McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report, cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-performing organizations can achieve an EBITDA uplift of 20-30% by 2030.
According to McKinsey's report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted $42.2 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, according to Amazon's Q2 2026 results announcement.
AWS's Q2 2026 revenue growth of 37% was its fastest revenue growth since 2021, accelerating from 28% growth in the prior quarter.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) grew triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, per Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results (quarter ended June 30, 2026).
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, up from an earlier $180-190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice during 2026.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year.
Oracle's RPO growth was driven by large-scale AI infrastructure contracts, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
According to ResearchAndMarkets, hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310-330B by 2030.
According to Mordor Intelligence, 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending across software, hardware, and services is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Pulumi's Superintelligence Infrastructure page argues AI workloads from pre-training to inference require dynamic infrastructure orchestration rather than static configuration.
Modern IaC integrates with third-party services including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Policies uses AI-driven optimization to help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner predicts total spending on securing AI will reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said AI 'doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization.'
According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: 'Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications.'
Large tech companies are the first adopters of platform engineering practices.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal today; Pulumi's report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than toward faster dashboards and alerting alone.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
The CNCF Q3 2025 report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, and Kubernetes is often used as the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration across edge and core clusters.
Kubernetes will continue its ascent in 2027.
AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.
According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens has launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.

Pulumi released Pulumi Agent Skills, a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server providing infrastructure access to AI assistants, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Merging modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The post's framing that 2027 cloud infrastructure turns on AI agents moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes.
The post was last updated on 2026-09-15.
